title: 1991 AHSME 29
statement: Equilateral triangle \(ABC\) has been creased and folded so that vertex \(A\) now rests at \(A'\) on \(BC\) as shown. If \(BA'=1\) and \(A'C=2,\) then the length of crease \(PQ\) is

solutions.text:
With the coordinates in the hint, the perpendicular-bisector condition for \(X=(x,y)\) is \(|X-A|=|X-A'|,\) which simplifies to \[ x+3\sqrt3\,y=8. \] Intersecting this line with \(AB,\ y=\sqrt3x,\) gives \(P=(\frac{4}{5},\frac{4\sqrt3}{5}).\) Intersecting it with \(AC,\ y=\sqrt3(3-x),\) gives \(Q=(\frac{19}{8},\frac{5\sqrt3}{8}).\) Hence \[ \begin{aligned} PQ &=\sqrt{\left(\frac{63}{40}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{7\sqrt3}{40}\right)^2}\\ &=\frac7{20}\sqrt{21}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: A fold crease is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining a point to its image
